label: ILLUSTRATIVE: modelling guidance, not forecasts
scope: Used only by LIVE EXPLORE; never read by the Blind Replay pipeline or any as_of-gated path.
description: Guard-rails for LIVE EXPLORE (issue #61): when the model reads today's news and suggests a stress scenario, these are the plausible sizes for each ScenarioShock field by news category. They are modelling choices for the SYNTHETIC demo business (MATH_MODEL §1, §10), not forecasts of what any event will do. A cited source supports only the order of magnitude it names; the exact min/default/max are modelling judgment.

units.delta_rate: Δr, decimal per year added to the base rate (0.0025 = +25bp)
units.delta: δ, fraction of base-store demand lost during the shock window (0.10 = -10%)
units.availability_during_outage: κ_t inside the outage window, fraction in [0, 1] (0 = primary supplier delivers nothing); κ_t = 1 outside the window
units.dependent_share: φ, fraction of base-store sales that depend on the affected supply, in [0, 1]
units.start_week: first shocked week t, integer in 1..T
units.recovery_weeks: ρ, weeks of linear recovery after the window, integer >= 0

mapping_to_scenario_shock.demand: DemandShock(delta = delta, start_week = start_week, end_week = start_week + duration_weeks - 1, recovery_weeks = recovery_weeks)
mapping_to_scenario_shock.supplier: SupplierOutage(availability = [availability_during_outage if start_week <= t <= start_week + duration_weeks - 1 else 1.0 for t = 1..T], dependent_share = dependent_share)

how_to_use: Classify the news into one category id (or none). Set only the shock blocks that category lists. For each parameter, clamp the model's suggestion to [min, max] (week fields are integers); if the model gives no value, use default. Every window, including recovery, then ends by week T. The human confirms or edits the result before /api/simulate runs; the numbers are inputs, never forecasts.
worse_when_meaning: Direction in which the parameter makes the stress scenario more severe for cash: 'higher', 'lower', or null when timing has no fixed direction (moving a window changes which weeks fall inside the horizon).

categories.name: Central-bank rate surprise
categories.news_trigger: The central bank raises its policy rate by more than expected, or signals faster hikes than markets priced.
categories.timing_guidance: Start at the floating loan's next reset (week 1 if it resets weekly); at most about one meeting gap later (52 / 8 meetings = 6.5 weeks). No recovery within the horizon: the higher rate stays.
categories.rationale: Policy moves come in 25bp steps and 75bp was the largest single move of 2022-2025, and a floating loan reprices on the whole move, so a rate rise not in the baseline is +25 to +100bp on the floating term loan.
categories.basis: sourced order of magnitude; exact range is modelling judgment

sources.title: Open Market Operations (federal funds target range history)
sources.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.supports: Of the 17 target-range changes listed for 2022-2025, 10 were 25bp; the largest single moves were 75bp (Jun 16, Jul 28, Sep 22 and Nov 3, 2022).

sources.title: Meeting calendars, statements, and minutes
sources.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.supports: The FOMC holds eight regularly scheduled meetings a year, which bounds the start-week delay at about one meeting gap.

categories.name: Inflation surprise
categories.news_trigger: A consumer-price release comes in hotter than expected and markets price more rate hikes.
categories.timing_guidance: The rate effect arrives with the next policy meeting (weeks 1-8); the demand squeeze is mild but long (8-16 weeks) as real incomes fall, then recovers over up to 6 weeks.
categories.rationale: A hot print raises expected policy rates by about one or more 25bp steps and squeezes real spending a little; food is a necessity, so the demand hit is kept small (1-5%).
categories.basis: sourced order of magnitude for the rate step; demand size and all timing are modelling judgment

sources.title: Open Market Operations (federal funds target range history)
sources.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.supports: Of the 17 target-range changes listed for 2022-2025, 10 were 25bp; the largest single moves were 75bp. It does not say how much any move was caused by inflation news.

categories.name: Regional economic slowdown
categories.news_trigger: Local layoffs, a plant closure, or a regional downturn reduce household spending in the stores' area.
categories.timing_guidance: Starts within the first 6 weeks, lasts 4-12 weeks, then customers return over up to 8 weeks.
categories.rationale: A fresh/deli format loses discretionary baskets first, so footfall can fall 5-25% for one to three months; 25% is a severe local downturn, not a typical one.

categories.name: Local disruption (severe weather, road closure)
categories.news_trigger: A storm, flood, snow event or major road closure near the stores keeps customers away and delays deliveries.
categories.timing_guidance: Short and sharp: 1-3 weeks of lost footfall with up to 2 weeks of recovery, and 1-2 weeks of partial deliveries. Use the same start week for the demand and supplier blocks.
categories.rationale: A weather event or closure can halve trade for a week or two but rarely lasts longer; deliveries from the primary distributor are delayed rather than stopped, so κ stays partial by default.

categories.name: Distributor strike or labour action
categories.news_trigger: Workers at the primary distributor or its warehouses strike, or a labour dispute halts its deliveries.
categories.timing_guidance: 1-4 weeks of outage; deliveries may continue at up to half volume with non-striking staff. Default φ is the business's own outage share (0.40 for the demo business).
categories.rationale: A strike stops the primary distributor's lines for days to weeks, so the share φ of sales on its lines is lost unless the backup supplier is used.

categories.name: Primary supplier insolvency
categories.news_trigger: The primary distributor files for bankruptcy, enters administration, or stops trading.
categories.timing_guidance: Longer than a strike: 3-12 weeks until a new primary supplier is on-boarded; a trading administrator may keep up to 30% of deliveries going. Default φ is the business's own outage share (0.40 for the demo business).
categories.rationale: Replacing a primary distributor means new terms, credit checks and delivery set-up, which takes weeks, not days.

categories.name: Food-safety recall of a product line
categories.news_trigger: A supplier recalls a product line the stores sell (for example a deli meat or produce item) on food-safety grounds.
categories.timing_guidance: Usually immediate (week 1); the line is off the shelf for 1-6 weeks. Here φ is the recalled line's share of sales, not the distributor share 0.40.
categories.rationale: A recall removes one product line rather than a whole distributor, so the lost share is small (2-15% of sales); the outage block is reused as 'share of sales pulled from the shelf'.

categories.name: Bank credit tightening
categories.news_trigger: Banks report tighter lending standards or wider loan spreads for small businesses, or the business's lender signals a repricing.
categories.timing_guidance: Wider spreads reach the business only when its loans reprice (renewal or a covenant step-up), so start later than a policy move (weeks 1-13). The rate shock raises the term-loan rate and the revolver rate alike.
categories.rationale: When banks tighten, spreads over their cost of funds widen; for a small borrower at renewal that is modelled as +25 to +150bp on its floating debt.
categories.basis: sourced direction (spreads widen when banks tighten); size and timing are modelling judgment

sources.title: July 2023 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey on Bank Lending Practices
sources.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.supports: Banks reported tightened standards on C&I loans, and tightening was most widely reported for spreads of loan rates over the cost of funds. The page gives no spread size in basis points.

excluded.reason: Its main effect is higher operating cost (O_t) and delivery cost, and ScenarioShock has no cost lever (opex is a business parameter). Mapping it to a demand drop alone would misstate the cash effect, so no faithful mapping exists.
This works through the gross margin g (or purchase cost), which is a business parameter, not a ScenarioShock field.

excluded.news_type: Minimum-wage rise or a strike by the business's own staff
excluded.reason: Payroll W_t is a business parameter, and cutting payroll is an optimizer decision (z_t); no ScenarioShock field changes it.

excluded.news_type: Bank cuts the business's credit line
excluded.reason: The revolver limit is a business parameter used by the optimizer; ScenarioShock cannot reduce it. Only the price side of credit tightening (wider spreads) maps, via the rate shock above.

excluded.news_type: Rate cuts or other favourable news
excluded.reason: LIVE EXPLORE suggests stress scenarios; every range above is adverse. A negative Δr is valid for RateShock but is not guidance for a stress test.
